# Fixed-source Markov rigidity and direction-specific critical-cap averaging

This note gives a limitation on a proposed contraction mechanism and a
proved extension of symmetry-based circuit selection. The extension needs
only one actual critical normal to be annihilated by an average of affine
fiber automorphisms; the whole centroid graph need not be affine.

## 1. A uniform stationary contraction fixing an interior point is an automorphism

Let K be a full-dimensional convex body, y in int K, and let T_r be finitely
many affine maps with T_r(K) subset K and T_r(y)=y. Let w_r>0 sum to1.
Suppose uniform volume on K is stationary:

    sum_r w_r (T_r)_#(1_K dx)=1_K dx.              (1)

Then every T_r maps K bijectively onto K and has determinant of absolute
value1.

Proof. Translate y to zero, and let p_K be the Minkowski gauge of K-y.
It is finite, continuous and nonnegative, and vanishes only at zero.
Since T_r now is linear and maps K into K,

    p_K(T_r x)<=p_K(x).

Stationarity makes the integral of the difference, averaged with the
strictly positive weights, equal zero. Every summand is nonnegative, so
its integral is zero. Continuity and full support of volume on K imply
p_K(T_r x)=p_K(x) on all of K, and positive homogeneity extends this to
all continuous vectors. T_r has zero kernel, since p_K vanishes only at
zero; it is therefore invertible. The gauge identity then gives T_r K=K.
Volume equality gives the determinant assertion.

The interior-fixed-point hypothesis matters. A triangle can be partitioned
into two affine image triangles sharing a boundary vertex, and their
area-weighted uniform measures reproduce the original uniform measure.
Both contractions fix that boundary vertex. Thus this lemma must not be
used at an arbitrary boundary point without an additional argument.

## 2. Consequence for actual fiber-preserving Markov maps

Let the full positive fibers K_z form an actual finite mixed family.
Suppose affine ambient maps

    T_r(z,x)=(z,A_r x+B_r z+c_r)

preserve its mixed measure in the stationary sense (1), and all fix one
point Y=(p,y) with y interior to K_p. Positive stationarity and closed
support imply T_r(S) subset S for each r. Because each map fixes the base,
stationarity holds separately on each uniform fiber.

Apply Section1 on K_p. It gives |det A_r|=1. On every other fiber the
inclusion T_r(K_z) subset K_z therefore preserves its full volume, so the
two compact convex bodies are equal. Every T_r is thus an exact
fiber-preserving affine automorphism. In particular such stationary
contractions do not provide new freedom beyond exact automorphisms.

If additionally sum_r w_r A_r=0, the centroid equations

    g_z=A_r g_z+B_r z+c_r

force g_z=(sum w_r B_r)z+sum w_r c_r. Hence a completely balanced
fiber-preserving stationary averaging mechanism automatically has an
affine centroid graph. It cannot be invoked to bypass nonaffine-center
obstructions by calling a contraction average 'mass preserving.'

## 3. A directional extension which does not require affine centroids

There is nevertheless a weaker, genuinely directional sufficient
condition. Assume T_r are exact affine fiber-preserving automorphisms,
all fixing the actual deepest source Y=(p,y). Suppose one regular
nonvertical critical cap through Y is

    H={a dot(z-p)+u dot(x-y)>=0}, u!=0,

and positive weights w_r summing to one satisfy

    sum_r w_r A_r^T u=0.                          (2)

No assertion sum w_r A_r=0 is made. The centroid graph may be nonaffine in
directions not detected by u.

**Directional selection theorem.** Under these assumptions, one can select
a regular critical positive circuit and an admissible nonnegative
normal-dependent convex potential of efficiency at least Gamma_d.

Proof. The preimage caps H_r=T_r^(-1)H remain globally critical and regular,
since each T_r preserves mixed volume and fixes Y. Their continuous
normals are A_r^T u and their integer normals are a+B_r^T u. Equation (2)
positively balances the continuous normals. The common own-fiber cap
volume is strictly between zero and |K_p|: zero would contradict that
the balanced caps cover the own fiber, while full volume would make all
nonzero continuous margins nonnegative on its interior and their positive
sum identically zero, also impossible. Thus every row has a proper own
section and positive total coarea. Remove redundant caps if needed to
obtain a subcircuit of at most d+1 rows.

Let g_z be the actual centroid of K_z. Each automorphism preserves it, so

    (I-A_r)g_z=B_r z+c_r.

Multiplying by u and averaging gives, by (2),

    u dot g_z=u dot(Bbar z+cbar),
    Bbar=sum w_r B_r, cbar=sum w_r c_r.             (3)

Thus the ONE centroid projection u dot g_z is affine, even though the
whole graph need not be. Similarly the fixed-source identities imply
u dot y=u dot(Bbar p+cbar). Consequently the affine base function

    m(z)=a dot(z-p)+u dot(g_z-y)
        =(a+Bbar^T u) dot(z-p)                    (4)

vanishes at p. Choose an exposed vertex e of conv(P) maximizing m, so
m(e)>=0.

Every preimage cap has the SAME value m(z) at the corresponding fiber
centroid: T_r(z,g_z)=(z,g_z). Thus every selected cap at e contains its
parallel through-g_e cap. Choose an affine function ell exposing e, and
choose a sufficiently large finite B. The potential

    Phi(n,z,x)=[n dot(x-g_e)+B ell(z)]_+            (5)

vanishes on all other actual fiber boundaries and equals radial velocity
about g_e on boundary K_e. Its denominator is d|K_e|. Its contribution for
each selected cap is at least the radial flux of the parallel
through-centroid cap, namely at least d Gamma_d |K_e| by ordinary
Grünbaum. Therefore every normalized response-weight choice on the
selected list pays Gamma_d. This includes the weights associated to its
positive circuit; no relation between w_r and these final normalized
weights is presumed.

The potential uses the fixed point g_e, not a nonlinear center field,
so it is physically convex even when other centroids are nonaffine.
Regularity means the full hyperplane-parameter coarea differentiability
specified in the selected-circuit source. Closed caps and supporting
endpoint traces are handled by inclusion, never by dropping boundary
mass or equating an offset cap volume with radial flux.

## 4. Scope and a concrete structural interpretation

For a common reflection group fixing a continuous subspace F, condition
(2) can hold for cap normals perpendicular to F, while centroids drift
nonaffinely inside F. Thus this is weaker than full affine-centroid
symmetry. It is conditional on an ACTUAL critical cap in such a direction;
no existence of that cap is asserted.

If all the relevant critical normals retain a nonzero component in the
common fixed subspace, the theorem supplies no balanced circuit. The
remaining directions and any nonsmooth allocation problem stay separate.
The general selected-circuit bound E_*(Y)>=Gamma_d remains unproved.
